requirements.title: Access and order of checks on a write route
requirements.rationale: A caller must get the same refusal, for the same reason, on every write route, and a refused write must leave no trace on the forge or in the event log.

criteria.condition: a write route is called with a PAT that lacks the scope `forge:write`, or by a caller whose access to the workspace is below write
criteria.action: refuse the request before it reads the body or the workspace state
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope` for a PAT without `forge:write`, also when the slug names no workspace; HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` for a caller with read access only, also when the workspace is archived; HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` for a caller with no access; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
an org workspace that a second user can read but not write, and an archived copy of it
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log

the write routes {POST issues, PATCH issues/7, POST issues/7/close, POST issues/7/comments, POST issues/7/labels, DELETE issues/7/labels/bug, POST labels, POST pulls, POST pulls/7/comments}, each with a valid body
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over every write route x the callers {PAT with `forge:read` only on `demo`, the same PAT on the unknown slug `nope`, a read-only org member on `demo`, the same member on an archived workspace, a user with no access}: r = call(route, caller); assert (r.status, r.json.error.error_type) == (403, 'insufficient_scope') for the two PAT rows, (403, 'forbidden') for the two member rows, (404, 'not_found') for the last; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0

criteria.condition: a write route is called by a caller with write access on a workspace whose status is `archived`
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with `error_type` `workspace_archived`; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded

setup: an archived GitHub workspace `old` with credential kind `pat` and the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log

the write routes {POST issues, PATCH issues/7, POST issues/7/close, POST issues/7/comments, POST issues/7/labels, DELETE issues/7/labels/bug, POST labels, POST pulls, POST pulls/7/comments}, each with a valid body
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over every write route: r = call(route, owner, slug='old'); assert r.status == 409 and r.json.error.error_type == 'workspace_archived'; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0

criteria.condition: a write route is called with the slug of a task fork by a caller who has write access on the fork's parent
criteria.action: carry out the write on the parent's forge repository, with the parent's stored credential and the parent's forge settings, including `target=upstream` when the parent is a carry-patch workspace with an `upstream_url`
criteria.contract: the answer is the one the same request gives on the parent's slug; the forge request names the parent's repository and carries the parent's token

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a task fork `demo-fork` of `demo` owned by the caller, with no credential and no forge settings of its own
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go: r = post('/workspaces/demo-fork/issues', {title:'t'}); assert r.status == 201; assert forge.last.path == '/repos/acme/widgets/issues' and forge.last.header('Authorization') carries the token of `demo`; repeat with a fork-bound PAT of the same user and assert 201

criteria.condition: a write route is called with the slug of a task fork and the caller has less than write access on the fork's parent, or the parent's status is `archived`
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` when the caller lacks write access on the parent; HTTP 409 with `error_type` `parent_archived` when the parent is archived and the caller has write access on it; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded

setup: an org workspace with a task fork owned by a member whose access to the parent is read only
an archived workspace with a task fork owned by the parent's owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over {fork owned by an org member who can only read the parent -> (403, 'forbidden'); fork of an archived parent, caller owns both -> (409, 'parent_archived'); fork of an archived parent, caller can only read the parent -> (403, 'forbidden')}: r = post('/workspaces/<fork>/issues', {title:'t'}); assert status and error_type; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0

criteria.condition: a write route passes every earlier check and the credential kind for the target is `none`
criteria.action: refuse the request without sending anything to the forge, including the lookup a label removal or a label ensure would begin with
criteria.contract: HTTP 422 with `error_type` `forge_credential_missing`; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded

setup: a GitHub workspace `anon` with no stored git credential and the caller as its owner
a GitHub workspace `basic` whose stored credential is a username and a password
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log

the write routes {POST issues, PATCH issues/7, POST issues/7/close, POST issues/7/comments, POST issues/7/labels, DELETE issues/7/labels/bug, POST labels, POST pulls, POST pulls/7/comments}, each with a valid body
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over every write route: r = call(route, owner, slug='anon'); assert r.status == 422 and r.json.error.error_type == 'forge_credential_missing'; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0; then the same table with a workspace whose credential kind is `basic`: assert the forge request carries the stored password as the token

criteria.action: for any write request that fails more than one check, answer with the failure that comes first in this order: `target`; path parameters and body rules that do not depend on the forge kind; archived workspace or archived parent; forge configuration; GitLab assignees rule and text limits; missing credential
criteria.contract: one error envelope whose status and `error_type` are those of the first failing check; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded

setup: workspaces owned by the caller for each row: archived, unknown forge (remote host `code.example.com`, no `forge_api_url`), a stored `forge_api_url` that is not a valid URL, GitHub without credential, GitLab without credential
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table of requests that each fail two checks, with the expected first: {target=bogus + malformed JSON -> (400, 'invalid_request') naming target; target=upstream on a non-carry-patch workspace + number '07' -> (400, 'workspace_mode_mismatch'); number '0' on an archived workspace -> (400, 'invalid_request') with message 'number must be a positive decimal integer'; malformed JSON on a workspace with an unknown forge -> (400, 'invalid_request'); blank title on an archived workspace -> (400, 'invalid_request'); archived workspace with an unknown forge -> (409, 'workspace_archived'); body of 65,537 characters on a workspace with an unknown forge -> (422, 'forge_unknown'); invalid `forge_api_url` + no credential -> (422, 'forge_api_url_invalid'); GitLab update with only `assignees` + no credential -> (400, 'invalid_request'); GitHub body of 65,537 characters + no credential -> (413, 'payload_too_large'); target given twice -> (400, 'invalid_request')}: assert status and error_type per row; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0

criteria.condition: a write route is called with `target=upstream` on a carry-patch workspace that has an `upstream_url`
criteria.action: carry out the write on the upstream repository, through the API URL of `upstream_forge_api_url` or the default of the upstream host, with the upstream git credential or, when none is stored, the origin credential
criteria.contract: the forge request names the upstream repository and carries the upstream token; the recorded event has metadata `target` `upstream`; without `target`, or with `target=origin`, the request names the origin repository and the event has `target` `origin`

setup: a carry-patch GitHub workspace `cp` with origin `acme/widgets`, upstream `upstream/project`, both API URL settings pointing at the test forge and the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over {target absent, target=origin, target=upstream with an upstream credential, target=upstream with only the origin credential}: r = post('/workspaces/cp/issues' + query, {title:'t'}); assert r.status == 201; assert forge.last.path names `acme/widgets` for the origin rows and `upstream/project` for the upstream rows; assert the token sent is the upstream one, or the origin one in the last row; assert events.last.metadata.target equals the target of the row

requirements.title: Write bodies and text limits
requirements.rationale: A body the forge would reject or truncate is refused by the hub with a message that names the field, before any request leaves.

criteria.condition: the body of a write route is not valid JSON, is not a JSON object on a route that takes an object, or is not a JSON array on the add-labels route
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over the routes that require a body {POST issues, PATCH issues/7, POST issues/7/comments, POST labels, POST pulls, POST pulls/7/comments} x the bodies {`{` (malformed), `[]`, `"x"`, `5`, none}, plus POST issues/7/labels x {`{`, `{}`, `"bug"`, none} and POST issues/7/close x {`{`, `[]`, `5`}: assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0

criteria.condition: a field of a write body breaks its rule: a required string is absent, null or blank; a field has the wrong JSON type; a list of names has more than 100 entries, a blank entry or an entry that is not a string; the add-labels array is empty; `state` is neither `open` nor `closed`; `color` is not six hex digits with or without a leading `#`
criteria.action: refuse the request and name the offending field in the message
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request` and a `message` that contains the field's name; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table of (route, body, field): {POST issues: no title, title null, title '  ', title 5, labels 'bug', labels of 101 names, labels ['a',''], labels ['a',5], assignees of 101 names, body 5}; {PATCH issues/7: title '', title ' \t', state 'merged', state 5, labels [' ']}; {POST issues/7/close: comment 5}; {POST issues/7/comments and POST pulls/7/comments: no body, body '', body ' ', body null}; {POST issues/7/labels: [], 101 names, ['a',' '], ['a',5]}; {POST labels: no name, name ' ', color 'red', color '#12345', color 'ededed0', color 5, description 5}; {POST pulls: no title, no head, no base, head ' ', draft 'yes'}: assert r.status == 400 and r.json.error.error_type == 'invalid_request' and r.json.error.message contains field; assert forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0. Boundary rows that must pass validation: labels of exactly 100 names, a 100-name add-labels array, color '#EDEDED', color 'abcdef'

criteria.action: for any write body, treat a member whose value is `null` exactly as an absent member and ignore members it does not know
criteria.contract: the forge request and the answer are the same as for the body without those members

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table of body pairs (plain, decorated): POST issues {title:'t'} vs {title:'t', body:null, labels:null, assignees:null, extra:1}; POST pulls {title,head,base} vs the same with body:null, draft:null, extra:{}; POST labels {name:'n'} vs {name:'n', color:null, description:null, x:1}; PATCH issues/7 {title:'t'} vs {title:'t', body:null, state:null, labels:null}: send each, assert both answers have the same status and that the two recorded forge request bodies are equal

criteria.condition: a measured text (the `body` of an issue create or update, of a comment or of a pull request, or the `comment` of a close) has more Unicode code points than the forge's limit: 65,536 on GitHub, 1,000,000 on GitLab
criteria.action: refuse the request before anything is sent
criteria.contract: HTTP 413 with `error_type` `payload_too_large` and a `message` that contains the field's name, the text's length in characters and the limit; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded; a text of exactly the limit is accepted and sent

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a GitLab workspace `gl` (remote `https://gitlab.com/group/sub/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/write_test.go, a table over the measured fields {POST issues body, PATCH issues/7 body, POST issues/7/comments body, POST pulls/7/comments body, POST pulls body, POST issues/7/close comment} x {GitHub with 65,536 ASCII characters -> success, GitHub with 65,537 -> 413, GitHub with 65,536 two-byte characters -> success, GitLab with 65,537 -> success}, plus GitLab POST issues body with 1,000,000 ASCII characters -> success and 1,000,001 -> 413: for the 413 rows assert error_type == 'payload_too_large', message contains the field name, the length ('65537' or '1000001') and the limit ('65536' or '1000000'), forge.requests == 0 and events.count == 0; for the success rows assert a 2xx status and that the forge received the text unchanged

requirements.title: Create and update an issue
requirements.rationale: An agent files and maintains issues without a forge credential (FRG-US-02).

criteria.condition: a caller with write access submits POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/issues with a non-blank `title` and optional `body`, `labels` and `assignees`
criteria.action: create the issue on the forge with the fields that are set and answer with the issue the forge returns
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the issue (`number`, `title`, `body`, `state`, `url`, `author`, `labels`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `closed_at`, `is_pr`); the forge received one create request carrying the stored token

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a GitLab workspace `gl` (remote `https://gitlab.com/group/sub/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/issue_write_test.go, a table over {GitHub, GitLab} x the bodies {{title}, {title, body, labels:['bug','p1'], assignees:['ann']}}: r = post('/workspaces/<slug>/issues', body); assert r.status == 201 and r.json.number == 7 and r.json.title == body.title and r.json.state == 'open' and r.json.is_pr == false; assert forge.requests == 1; on GitHub assert the request is POST /repos/acme/widgets/issues with exactly the set fields; on GitLab assert it is POST /projects/group%2Fsub%2Fwidgets/issues with `description` for body and `labels` 'bug,p1'

criteria.condition: a caller with write access submits PATCH /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/issues/:number with at least one of `title`, `body`, `state`, `labels` and `assignees` set
criteria.action: send only the set fields to the forge, where `body` `""` clears the body, `labels` and `assignees` each replace the whole set and `[]` clears it, and `state` is `open` or `closed`, and answer with the issue as the forge returns it
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the issue; the forge received one update request holding the set fields and no others

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a GitLab workspace `gl` (remote `https://gitlab.com/group/sub/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/issue_write_test.go, a table over {GitHub, GitLab} x the bodies {{title:'new'}, {body:''}, {state:'closed'}, {state:'open'}, {labels:[]}, {labels:['a','b']}, {assignees:[]} (GitHub only), {title:'new', body:'b', state:'closed', labels:['a'], assignees:['ann']}}: r = patch('/workspaces/<slug>/issues/7', body); assert r.status == 200 and r.json equals the issue the test forge returned; assert forge.requests == 1; on GitHub assert PATCH /repos/acme/widgets/issues/7 whose JSON members are exactly the set fields (body '' and labels [] present, not dropped); on GitLab assert PUT /projects/group%2Fsub%2Fwidgets/issues/7 with `description`, `state_event` 'close' or 'reopen', and `labels` as one comma-separated string ('' for [])

criteria.condition: an update's body sets none of `title`, `body`, `state`, `labels` and `assignees`
criteria.action: refuse the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; the forge receives no request and no event is recorded

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would

criteria.condition: the forge kind of the target is `gitlab`
criteria.action: leave `assignees` out of the request it sends for an issue create or update and send the other set fields

requirements.title: Close an issue
requirements.rationale: Closing with a reason is one call, and a failure half way leaves a record of what was already posted.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access submits POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/issues/:number/close with no body, an empty body, `{}`, `{"comment": null}` or a blank `comment`
criteria.action: close the issue on the forge without posting a comment, also when the issue is already closed, and answer with the issue
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the issue, whose `state` is `closed`; the forge received exactly one request, the close

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a GitLab workspace `gl` (remote `https://gitlab.com/group/sub/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/issue_write_test.go, a table over {GitHub, GitLab} x the bodies {none, empty, `{}`, `{"comment":null}`, `{"comment":"  "}`} x {issue open, issue already closed}: r = post('/workspaces/<slug>/issues/7/close', body); assert r.status == 200 and r.json.state == 'closed'; assert forge.requests == 1 and it is the close (GitHub PATCH issues/7 {state:'closed'}; GitLab PUT issues/7 {state_event:'close'}); assert events.last has no `comment_url`

criteria.condition: a caller with write access submits the close route with a non-blank `comment`
criteria.action: post the comment on the issue first and, after the forge accepted it, close the issue and answer with the issue
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the closed issue; the forge received the comment request and then the close request, in that order; the `parley.forge.issue.close` event has `ok` true and `comment_url` equal to the comment's web URL

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a GitLab workspace `gl` (remote `https://gitlab.com/group/sub/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that records every request it receives and answers as GitHub or GitLab would

criteria.condition: the forge refuses or fails the comment of a close
criteria.action: answer with the comment's failure and send no close request
criteria.contract: the status and `error_type` that the comment's failure maps to; the issue's state on the forge is unchanged; exactly one `parley.forge.issue.close` event is recorded with `ok` false, that `error_type` and no `comment_url`

setup: a GitHub workspace `demo` (remote `https://github.com/acme/widgets.git`, credential kind `pat`, `forge_api_url` pointing at the test forge) with the caller as its owner
the test forge fails the comment request with the status of the row
an event recorder in place of the event log
check.pseudocode: in internal/forge/issue_write_test.go, a table over the comment answers {404 -> (404, 'forge_not_found'), 422 -> (422, 'forge_rejected'), 500 -> (502, 'forge_error')}: r = post('/workspaces/demo/issues/7/close', {comment:'c'}); assert status and error_type; assert forge.requests == 1 (no close was sent); assert events.count == 1 and events.last.metadata.ok == false and events.last.metadata.error_type == error_type and 'comment_url' not in events.last.metadata

the test forge accepts the comment and fails the close request with the status of the row

requirements.title: Comment on an issue or a pull request
requirements.rationale: An agent reports progress where people read it.

criteria.condition: a caller with write access submits POST /api/v1/workspaces/:slug/issues/:number/comments with a non-blank `body`
criteria.action: post the text, exactly as given, as a comment on that issue

requirements.title: CLI commands for forge writes
requirements.rationale: The CLI is how most agents reach the hub; every write route has one command.

criteria.condition: a user runs one of `parley issue create`, `parley issue update`, `parley issue close`, `parley issue comment`, `parley label create`, `parley pr create` and `parley pr comment` with valid arguments
criteria.action: send the command's route once with a JSON body holding only the fields whose flags were given and with `target` in the query only when `--target` was given, and print the hub's answer
criteria.contract: stdout is the hub's answer as one JSON document; exit status 0, for `parley label create` both when the hub answers 200 and when it answers 201; the request is: issue create -> POST /api/v1/workspaces/<slug>/issues {title, body, labels, assignees}; issue update -> PATCH …/issues/<number> {title, body, state, labels, assignees}; issue close -> POST …/issues/<number>/close with no body, or {comment} with `--comment`; issue comment -> POST …/issues/<number>/comments {body}; label create -> POST …/labels {name, color, description}; pr create -> POST …/pulls {title, head, base, body, draft}; pr comment -> POST …/pulls/<number>/comments {body}; no `Idempotency-Key` header is sent

setup: a stub hub (`httptest` server) that records each request and answers the route's success status with a fixed body
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/issue_test.go, internal/cli/label_test.go and internal/cli/pr_test.go, a table of (argv, method, path, query, body): {issue create demo --title T -> POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/issues, {title:'T'}}; {issue create demo --title T --body B --label a --label b --assignee ann --target upstream -> query target=upstream, {title:'T', body:'B', labels:['a','b'], assignees:['ann']}}; {issue update demo 7 --state closed -> PATCH …/issues/7 {state:'closed'}}; {issue update demo 7 --body '' -> {body:''}}; {issue update demo 7 --title N --label x -> {title:'N', labels:['x']}}; {issue close demo 7 -> POST …/issues/7/close, no body}; {issue close demo 7 --comment done -> {comment:'done'}}; {issue comment demo 7 --body hi -> POST …/issues/7/comments {body:'hi'}}; {label create demo type/bug -> POST …/labels {name:'type/bug'}}; {label create demo n --color '#00ff00' --description d -> {name:'n', color:'#00ff00', description:'d'}}; {pr create demo --title T --head f --base main -> POST …/pulls {title:'T', head:'f', base:'main'}}; {pr create demo --title T --head bob:f --base main --body B --draft -> {…, body:'B', draft:true}}; {pr comment demo 12 --body ok -> POST …/pulls/12/comments {body:'ok'}}: run the command against the stub hub; assert exactly one request with that method, path, query and JSON body and without an Idempotency-Key header; assert exit 0 and that stdout decodes to the stub's answer; for label create run once with the stub answering 200 and once 201 and assert exit 0 both times

execution_paths.title: An agent files, labels and comments on an issue from the shell

steps.action: runs `parley issue create demo --title "Flaky test" --label bug` with a PAT that has `forge:write`
sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/issues with the body {"title": "Flaky test", "labels": ["bug"]}
checks the scope, write access, the body, the workspace state, the forge configuration, the text limit and the credential kind
sends the create request to the forge's API with the workspace's stored token
records `parley.forge.issue.create` with `ok` true and answers 201 with the issue
prints the issue on stdout and exits 0
runs `parley issue label demo 1 triage` and `parley issue comment demo 1 --body-file -` with the text on standard input
adds the label and posts the comment on the forge, records `parley.forge.label.add` and `parley.forge.comment.create`, and answers 204 and 201
prints the `labeled` confirmation and the comment's `url`, and exits 0 each time

real_components: parley CLI commands `issue create`, `issue label` and `issue comment`
parleyd HTTP server with authentication, the scope check and the workspace access rule
forge configuration and forge client of package 41
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a secrets key and a forge transport that trusts the test forge
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that plays GitHub's REST API for one repository and requires the token
a test origin whose URL path is `/acme/widgets.git`, and the workspace `demo` created through POST /workspaces with `git_pat` and waited for until `ready`
the workspace setting `forge_api_url` set to the test forge's URL followed by `/github`
a PAT of the workspace's owner with the scope `forge:write`
end_state: the three commands exit 0; the first prints an issue with number 1, the second `{"status":"labeled","number":1,"labels":["triage"]}`, the third an object with a `url`
the test forge holds issue 1 with the labels `bug` and `triage` and one comment whose text equals standard input
every request the test forge received carried the stored token
the event log holds exactly three forge events for `demo`, of the types `parley.forge.issue.create`, `parley.forge.label.add` and `parley.forge.comment.create`, each with `ok` true
no command output and no event contains the stored token or the comment text
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/forge_write_test.go: forge = newGitHubForge(token); hub = startHub(forgeTransport: forge.client); create workspace demo with git_pat = token; waitReady; patch settings forge_api_url = forge.url + '/github'; out1, c1 = runCLI('issue', 'create', 'demo', '--title', 'Flaky test', '--label', 'bug'); out2, c2 = runCLI('issue', 'label', 'demo', '1', 'triage'); out3, c3 = runCLIStdin(text, 'issue', 'comment', 'demo', '1', '--body-file', '-'); assert c1 == c2 == c3 == 0; assert out1.number == 1 and out2 == {status:'labeled', number:1, labels:['triage']} and out3.url != ''; assert forge.issue(1).labels == ['bug','triage'] and forge.comments(1) == [text]; ev = eventsOf('demo', prefix 'parley.forge.'); assert types(ev) == ['parley.forge.issue.create','parley.forge.label.add','parley.forge.comment.create'] and all ok; assert token and text appear in none of out1..3 and no event

execution_paths.title: An agent retries opening a pull request and gets one pull request

steps.action: sends POST /api/v1/workspaces/demo/pulls with `title`, `head`, `base` and the header `Idempotency-Key: pr-1`
runs the checks, finds no record for the key and sends the create request to the forge with the workspace's stored token
opens pull request 1 and returns it
records `parley.forge.pull_request.create` with `head`, `base`, `draft` and `ok` true, stores the answer under the key and answers 201
does not receive the answer and sends the same request with the same key again
finds the record and answers 200 with the first answer, without contacting the forge and without recording an event
posts the comment in the pull request's conversation, records `parley.forge.pull_request.comment` and answers 201 with the comment's `url`

real_components: parleyd HTTP server with authentication, the scope check, the workspace access rule and the idempotency records
forge configuration and forge client of package 41
setup: a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a secrets key and a forge transport that trusts the test forge
a test forge (`httptest` TLS server) that plays GitHub's REST API for one repository, holds the branches `main` and `feature`, and counts the requests it receives
the workspace `demo` created through POST /workspaces with `git_pat`, waited for until `ready`, with `forge_api_url` set to the test forge's URL followed by `/github`
a PAT of the workspace's owner with the scope `forge:write`
end_state: the first answer is 201 and the second 200, with equal bodies whose `number` is 1
the test forge holds exactly one pull request, from `feature` to `main`, and received exactly one create request for it
the test forge holds one comment on pull request 1
the event log holds exactly one `parley.forge.pull_request.create` event and one `parley.forge.pull_request.comment` event for `demo`, both with `ok` true
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/forge_write_test.go: forge = newGitHubForge(token, branches: ['main','feature']); hub = startHub(forgeTransport: forge.client); create workspace demo; waitReady; set forge_api_url; body = {title:'Add feature', head:'feature', base:'main'}; r1 = post('/workspaces/demo/pulls', body, header Idempotency-Key 'pr-1'); r2 = the same again; assert r1.status == 201 and r2.status == 200 and r2.json == r1.json and r1.json.number == 1; assert len(forge.pulls) == 1 and forge.count('POST', '/repos/acme/widgets/pulls') == 1; r3 = post('/workspaces/demo/pulls/1/comments', {body:'ready for review'}); assert r3.status == 201 and r3.json.url != ''; assert forge.comments(1) == ['ready for review']; ev = eventsOf('demo', prefix 'parley.forge.'); assert types(ev) == ['parley.forge.pull_request.create','parley.forge.pull_request.comment'] and all ok
